what: Juno on her hoverboard, shooting under a closing blast door: the moment she beats the machines chasing her, and she knows it. Both drawings are seen from her LEFT side and a little from in FRONT, at the height of her face; she moves toward the viewer's LEFT, and her FACE is turned toward the viewer's left and a little toward the viewer, so her whole face shows in near profile: eyebrows, a wide bright eye, nose, and a huge grin. Her face is the point of both drawings: it is never hidden, never turned down, never covered by an arm, a hand, her hair or the board. Her round goggles sit pushed up on her forehead (not over her eyes); her one long side lock and her hair stream straight back behind her (toward the viewer's right). Drawing 1 (top), DROPPING: folded right down over the board in the deepest crouch, chest on her knees, both hands reaching down to grip the board's front edge, chin lifted, eyes locked on the gap ahead, a wide open-mouthed delighted grin. Drawing 2 (bottom), FLAT: she lies on her front, full length, ON the hoverboard (this mannequin has no green slab: draw the board flat under her chest and belly: the same flat plank of welded pale steel-grey scrap-metal plates, with two small blue thruster pods under it, each with its short flat cyan flame; it has NO wheels), propped on her elbows with her CHIN UP, well clear of the board, head lifted and looking straight ahead at the gap, teeth showing in a fierce gleeful grin, both gloved hands gripping the board's nose out in front of her, below her chin, legs stretched straight out behind her with the toes pointed, as flat and low as she can make herself. The board in both drawings is plain bare metal plates with rivets: NO letters, no numbers, no symbols, no scratches that look like writing anywhere on it. The WHOLE figure, from the hands and the tip of the hair to the toes and the end of the board, is inside its own half of the sheet with clear magenta all round it; nothing is cut off.
